description: PROVISIONAL DATA ONLY. This manifest is local to docs/scopes. It is not registered in the packages/workbay-system eval registry, which is absent from this checkout; when that registry lands, it needs an EXECUTOR_BY_SUITE_ID entry or a local runner. Describe-time naming cases live in scene/tests (scene owns describe); the PHP guardrail case runs under php_command. There is one case per success criterion in public-figure-library-scope.md. The tests are deliverables of the RED lane. PFL-SC-12 is an offline VM benchmark and does not run under the deterministic command.
command: cd apps/prototype-description-service && uv run --locked --extra dev pytest -q recognition/tests/unit/test_pfl_candidates.py recognition/tests/unit/test_pfl_lifecycle.py recognition/tests/unit/test_pfl_audit.py recognition/tests/api/test_pfl_isolation.py recognition/tests/api/test_pfl_accept.py scene/tests/test_pfl_naming.py scene/tests/test_pfl_name_resolution.py

cases.criterion: Default-off: no entitlement or no tenant opt-in yields zero PFL candidates.
A mismatch between probe and template embedding_model yields zero PFL candidates. It fails closed, not with an error.
Templates are never served when the reference capture_basis or licence is null or unrecognised.
Identities outside the tenant's enabled tiers, flagged as minors, or opted out are never served.

Below the floor the result is unknown. The possible band is suggestion-only. The strong band auto-names only when the gate passes: tenant auto-name on, tier enabled, tier calibrated, context public_role. Otherwise it is a suggestion.
At equal band, a tenant roster candidate outranks a PFL candidate. A PFL name never overwrites a tenant's own (non-PFL) person label.
No tenant probe, accept, or edit writes to PFL tables. An acceptance by tenant A is invisible to tenant B.
Link-on-accept stores the QID and provenance on the tenant cluster, never a name string.
A tombstone or opt-out removes the identity's templates from the served index and stops its name resolving in later descriptions for every tenant.
A linked PFL identity is not named in descriptions when allow_person_names is false.
Every PFL query writes an audit row recording tenant, gallery_version, and candidate count.

Before a tier (P1, P2, P3 or historical) is enabled or auto-name turns on for it: FMR/FNMR per skin-tone slice are within the parity bound on the gallery population and on news imagery, and FPIR at the served gallery size is within the operator's auto-name bound at the strong-band ceiling.
cases.test: benchmarks/pfl/fairness_slices (VM/GPU; operator sets the bound before Phase 1 enablement)

cases.criterion: The served gallery_version matches the active embedding contract. Stale versions are refused.
Every auto-named face carries pfl_auto provenance (QID, gallery_version, band) in naming_provenance. private or unclear context never auto-names.
'Not this person' unnames the identity in the tenant's later descriptions and suppresses re-auto-naming on that cluster.
P2 news-cycle lifecycle: entry above the salience threshold, exit after 90 days below it, templates deleted on exit. P1 membership follows Wikidata P39 end dates.

Names resolve from pfl.identity_name for the description language: exact locale, then base language, then canonical (es-MX → es 'Papa León XIV'; en 'Pope Leo XIV'). A registry edit changes the next description for every linked tenant.

Adding a language needs only registry rows and a supported_languages entry: enabling a fixture language (es) in test config yields 'Papa León XIV' with no code or schema change. A language below full verified coverage is refused at enable. A disabled or unknown language resolves to en.

P3 living-celebrity tier (decision 18981): a living adult above the notability threshold with a voluntary public career is served. Minors, relatives without independent notability, and involuntary newsmakers are never served, even above the threshold. A P3 strong-band match auto-names only in public_role context; private or unclear context yields a suggestion.
